knowledge.text: In the earlier single-pass family-sweep search edit, the Candidate found a clean butterknife on countertop2 and a clean soapbar on shelf1 after the Parent had exhausted drawers, cabinets, and the sink area without reaching those families; the Candidate thus succeeded where the Parent hit the step limit. The same version still timed out in a clean-butterknife task when no exact butterknife was found, with both sides cycling, and in a cool-apple pair both succeeded but the Candidate needed 46 steps versus the Parent's 38 while revisiting many already-seen empty locations. Across those ten pairs the Parent succeeded 7/10 and the Candidate 9/10 with no observed regression on Parent-solved tasks, but each task was run once, and the rescues depended on the exact target being present in an uninspected family.

The current follow-up diff further tightened the general search step: each individual closed container and each open surface is a separate candidate, already-open empty or matching locations should be left immediately, and a recurring small set of locations should be abandoned. Across the seven current pairs the Candidate succeeded 6/7 versus the Parent's 5/7 with no task-level success regression. In a cool-tomato-in-microwave task the Candidate avoided the Parent's repeated fridge/cabinet1/countertop1 moves and reached countertop2, succeeding in 10 steps versus 18; in a two-creditcard-to-safe task the Candidate went directly to the desk and finished in 9 steps versus 24 after the Parent opened drawers 1-8; in a two-book-to-desk task the Candidate eventually moved from repeated desk/drawer/shelf/sidetable visits to the bed and placed both books in 40 steps, while the Parent hit the 50-step limit still cycling. These outcomes are compatible with the clause enabling new-family or open-surface discovery and rescuing some prior failures, but the current diff was applied jointly with temperature guidance and each task was run once, so whole-task counts are not isolated causal estimates.

The strengthened search instruction was not reliably followed and did not prevent cycling. In one cool-plate task the Candidate opened empty cabinet1 before finding the plate, taking 9 steps versus the Parent's 8; in a heat-apple-to-diningtable pair both Parent and Candidate hit the 50-step limit while repeatedly moving among the fridge, countertop1/2, and cabinet1/2 and never reached the later cabinets, so the target was not found; in the two-book task the Candidate still revisited already-open empty drawers and shelves many times before finally going to the bed. Thus the clause can coexist with extra empty-container steps and with persistent step-limit cycling when the target is not located, and it is not a guarantee of efficient single-pass coverage.

Once the exact target was acquired, the rewritten temperature guidance was strongly associated with performing the explicit heat/cool action while holding the target at a closed appliance instead of inserting it and repeatedly toggling the door. In the current heat-tomato-to-fridge pair the Parent inserted the tomato and cycled the microwave door repeatedly before heating, succeeding in 39 steps, whereas the Candidate heated the held tomato at the closed microwave and placed it in 8; in a second heat-tomato pair the Candidate heated at the closed microwave and finished in 7 steps versus the Parent's 8 after opening the microwave. In a cool-plate pair the Candidate cooled the held plate at the closed fridge, but total steps were 9 versus the Parent's 8 because the Candidate added an empty-cabinet search visit, so the local appliance saving did not translate into a whole-task saving. Historical cool-pot, hot-apple, heat-egg, hot-potato, and heat-tomato pairs showed the same pattern of fewer appliance manipulations and steps when the exact target was found. This supports a robust local reduction in appliance manipulation conditional on acquiring the exact target, but not automatic whole-task savings when other phases differ.

The temperature guidance did not create success when the exact target was not located. In the current heat-apple-to-diningtable pair both Parent and Candidate hit the 50-step limit without an apple being found in the observed search or any heat action being performed. In a historical heat-plate pair the Parent found the plate and succeeded in 13 steps while the Candidate never reached that countertop and hit the limit; in a hot-mug pair the exact mug was not found in the observed search and both hit the limit, with the Candidate not taking or heating the visible cup substitute while the Parent took and heated a cup but still timed out. The observed benefit is therefore conditional on locating and acquiring the exact target; search failure and step-budget exhaustion remain outside what this clause resolves.
